source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 9, Schedule 1 Line 44; PDF page 10 ('Military retirement pay ... fully exempt'); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 95,000.00 + military retirement pay 60,000.00 = 155,000.00. Federal taxable income = 155,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 123,500.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 155,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 155,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 44 military retirement pay: fully exempt, no income test -> 60,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 60,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 60,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 155,000.00 - 60,000.00 = 95,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 95,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 95,000.00 is more than 71,000.00, exemption 0.00; Line 3 taxable income = 95,000.00 - 0.00 = 95,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 95,000.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 75,000.00 x 0.045 = 400.00 + 3,375.00 = 3,775.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 95,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 3,775.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 95,000.00 is in the band more than 52,000.00); Line 9 = 3,775.00 x 0.10 = 377.50. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 3,775.00 - 377.50 = 3,397.50 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Federal AGI 155,000 is past the end of the Line 48b phase-out (150,000 MFJ); military retirement pay is subtracted in full anyway on Line 44 and is not part of the Line 48b worksheet.
